cultural.vision_reason: A gilded bronze figure of four-armed, four-faced Brahma wearing a Khmer-style sampot with fish-tail drape, consistent with Khmer temple bronze casting traditions; this is court/temple art made within the culture.

physical.title: figure
physical.summary: Standing figure of a crowned Brahma with four arms and four faces wearing a Khmer-style sampot (skirt-cloth). Brahma is holding a conch shell in his upper right hand and a libation jar in his upper left. The lower two hands once held other attributes, which are now missing. He wears bracelets, armlets and a necklace, which are not elaborately depicted but are gilded. His sampot has a fish-tail shape in the front and back. Only the belt and the central sections in the front and back are gilded. The crown is composed of three concentric layers and a finial, with broad headbands across the forehead surmounted by a central boss. The long sides of the headdress that dangle nearly to the shoulder conclude in lotus bud shapes. Made of cast bronze with some lacquer and gilding.
